newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico exports seen up 11.7 pct in 1997 -- Banamex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico exports seen up 11.7 pct in 1997 -- Banamex.

text.p: Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival expects the country's exports to grow by 11.7 percent in 1997, the bank said in a monthly report issued on Monday.
"The total (value of exports) at the end of the year is $95 billion, and for 1997, we estimate $106 billion," the report said.
The dollar value of Mexican exports in 1996 grew by 19 percent from 1995, when exports amounted to $79.542 billion, the bank said.
The report said agricultural exports would increase by eight percent in 1997 and that crude oil exports would fall by two percent, largely because of lower world petroleum prices.
The report forecast 16.8 percent growth in imports next year, to $103.063 billion from $88.244 billion in 1996. In 1995, imports were valued at $72.453 billion, the report said.
